dossier.public_summary: The 0.91-day, 1,190 ppm dip repeats on the K-dwarf target and is planet-sized, but it shows a very deep secondary dip near phase 0.5 and a large out-of-eclipse brightness swing. The duration is ~74% longer than expected for a planet and requires a grazing impact geometry inconsistent with the star's density. Together this is the signature of a grazing eclipsing binary on the target, not a planet.

reasons.why: Second dip near phase 0.5 is deeper than primary and almost as strong; a planet should show no secondary above noise, only a hot Jupiter could show a tiny occultation. Here depth_over_dip 0.7286 and secondary_over_bump 1.027 favor stellar eclipse, not planetary.

Large out-of-eclipse modulation comparable to dip depth indicates ellipsoidal/beaming and spot signal from a close binary, not a small planet. Rotation amplitude 5008-13856 ppm in sectors 44,70,71 and variability_chi2_dof 35.65 support stellar variability.

Duration 1.74x longer than central transit and fitted b 0.7471 with negative density ratio indicate grazing/large-star eclipse. TIC density penalty dominates fit_chi2_red 1.069, inconsistent with a planet transiting a 0.4238 Rsun M dwarf.
